question: The period from ———— is referred to as a period of stagnant or stationary phase of growth of India's population.
solution: The correct answer is __**1901-1921**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • The period **1901-1921** is referred to as the **stagnant or stationary phase** of India's population growth. • During this phase, the **population growth rate was almost negligible** due to high birth and death rates balancing each other. • India experienced frequent **famines, epidemics, and pandemics** like the influenza pandemic of 1918-19, which caused significant loss of life. • The absence of modern healthcare, sanitation, and public health measures further contributed to the **high mortality rate** during this time. • This phase is marked by a **low and fluctuating population growth rate**, which is why it is termed as the stagnant phase.
